texts.orig: The above result can easily be mis/-interpreted to say that the packet WFQ discipline and the /#0Duid GPS discipline provide almost identical service except for a di/#0Berence of one packet/. Contrary to this popular /#28but incorrect/#29 belief/, we will demonstrate that there could be large discrepancies between the services provided by WFQ and GPS/. In fact/, what has been proven is that WFQ cannot fall behind GPS by one maximum size packet/. However/, WFQ can be far ahead of GPS in terms of number of bits served for a session/. Since many congestion control algorithms /#5B/9/, /1/4/#5D were de/signed with the assumption that WFQ will provide almost identical service with GPS/, large discrepancies between the two disciplines and the lack of knowledge that such discrepancies exist will result in unstable and less e/#0Ecient network control algorithms/.

texts.orig: Notice that GPS is an idealized server that does not transmit packets as entities/. It assumes that the server can serve all backlogged sessions simultaneously and that the tra/#0Ec is in/#0Cnitely divisible/. In a more realistic packet system/, only one session can receive service at a time and an entire packet must be served before another packet can be served/. There are di/#0Ber/ent ways of emulating GPS service in a packet system/. The most popular one is the Weighted Fair Queueing discipline /#28WFQ/#29 /#5B/4/#5D/, also known as Packet General/ized Processor Sharing or PGPS /#5B/1/3/#5D/.
